claim_verdicts.evidence: Round 3: s2 now "no `orders` table in its own database"; ledger "no orders table in donhang_notifications". DonHang.Notifications.csproj has one ProjectReference, DonHang.Messaging; Messaging.csproj:11-14 "It knows no order, payment or email". docker-compose.yml:316 `Database=donhang_notifications`. Read from checked-out submodule; git show at stage-3 not permitted.

Round 2: s4 now says only "ran in one process and shared the donhang database, where emails were rows in the notifications table"; diagram N1 "Email code, same process". ADR 0002 l.12-15: at stage-2 emails were rows in table `notifications` of `donhang`, written by QueuedNotifier in the order's transaction, NotificationSender ran in every replica of DonHang.Api.

Unchanged from round 1. MS Learn internal: "You can access internal types or members only within files in the same assembly"; "It's an error to reference a type or a member with internal access outside the assembly where you defined it." Product, CatalogDbContext, EfProductRepository, ProductCache, CatalogService are `internal sealed`; no InternalsVisibleTo in repo.

Unchanged from round 1. ModuleBoundaryTests.cs:16-21 ProjectsCatalogMustNotUse = DonHang.Domain, DonHang.Infrastructure, DonHang.Api; 26-31 CatalogPublicTypes = CatalogModule, CatalogProduct, ICatalog; CatalogMakesPublicOnlyItsContract `Assert.Equal(CatalogPublicTypes, exported)`.

Round 2: new s5 sentence and q4.b rely on this. ModuleBoundaryTests.cs:59-69 ServiceUsesNoDonHangProjectButMessaging (InlineData OrderEventsConsumer, RefundRequestedConsumer) filters referenced assemblies `name.StartsWith("DonHang.") && name != "DonHang.Messaging"` and asserts empty. A project reference is loaded into the referencing process, which no network check sees.

Unchanged from round 1. OrderService.cs:33-37 `var price = await prices.CurrentPriceAsync(item.ProductId)` inside PlaceOrderAsync; CatalogProductPrices(ICatalog catalog) : IProductPrices; ICatalog implemented in-process by CatalogService.

Unchanged from round 1. OrderMessage.cs:3-6 "keeps its own copy of the shape instead of referencing DonHang.Domain: the JSON is the contract between the two, not a shared class." `record OrderMessage(int OrderId, string CustomerEmail, string CustomerName, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt)`, no product field.

Unchanged from round 1. RabbitMQ Queues: "A queue in RabbitMQ is an ordered collection of messages"; "Durable queues will be recovered on node boot, including messages in them published as persistent." Notifications RabbitMqTopology.cs:25 durable: true; RabbitMqPublisher.cs:28 Persistent = true.

Round 2: s4 now attributes the list to the ADR ("ADR 0002 counts one more image, build pipeline, database and dashboard to run for Notifications alone"). ADR 0002 l.43-45: "Thêm một image, một pipeline build, một database và một dashboard phải chạy. Gọi qua mạng có thể lỗi; ... email đến sau một lúc."
Round 2: s4 now reads "a service can be built, released, scaled and stopped on its own", a possibility of the style, consistent with release.yml releasing all images together and with outline item 4.

Unchanged from round 1. STAGE.md:13-16 "A modular monolith with two services split off, as at `stage-3`: `DonHang.Api` holds Ordering ... and Catalog ...; `DonHang.Notifications` and `DonHang.Payments` each own a database." ADRs 0002, 0003.

Round 2: services row last cell now "images, a database, and the build and monitoring for each service", matching the repo (two images per service, shared ci.yml) without claiming one dashboard each. q3.b and q5.c now say "more to build, run and watch".

Round 2: s7 now "would put another process, one that can be down or slow on its own, inside the step that takes orders". Consistent with the in-process call already going through ProductCache (Redis) and CatalogDbContext; the claim is about the added process only.
Unchanged from round 1. Design positions taken from the outline's three misconceptions, supported in s8 by ModuleBoundaryTests and ADRs 0002/0003; no pinned-version behaviour.

Round 3: s9 ans 3 now "Notifications' config names only its own database". Program.cs:16 GetConnectionString("Default") only; docker-compose.yml:316 ConnectionStrings__Default `Database=donhang_notifications`, :158 api same host/user/password with `Database=donhang`. PG 17 22.1: "clients can open multiple connections to the same database, or different databases." order_items: product_id, quantity, price; no name.
